title: Encore of Episode 9: Aziz Ansari on Modern Love

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, Aziz Ansari.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，阿齐兹·安萨里。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: Last year, I was asked to host an event in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 去年，我受邀在华盛顿特区主持一场活动，

sentences.en: with the comedian Aziz Ansari.
sentences.zh: 嘉宾是喜剧演员阿齐兹·安萨里。

sentences.en: You might know him as Tom Haverford from Parks and Recreation,
sentences.zh: 你可能在《公园与游憩》中认识他饰演的汤姆·哈弗福德，

sentences.en: or you might be binge-watching his original series on Netflix, Master of None.
sentences.zh: 或者你正在Netflix上刷他的原创剧集《无为大师》。

sentences.en: What you might not know is that Aziz is also interested in human behavior.
sentences.zh: 你可能不知道的是，阿齐兹也对人类行为很感兴趣。

sentences.en: He's thought about how social norms have changed the way people get together.
sentences.zh: 他思考过社会规范是如何改变人们相处方式的。

sentences.en: He's studied how romantic preferences have changed over time.
sentences.zh: 他研究过浪漫偏好是如何随时间演变的。

sentences.en: And he's examined how online dating is linked to the psychological phenomenon known as the paradox of choice.
sentences.zh: 他还审视过在线约会与心理学现象“选择悖论”之间的联系。

sentences.en: Like, there's just too much goddamn jam out there.
sentences.zh: 比如，市面上的果酱种类实在太多了。

sentences.en: Like, there's iPhone apps that literally tell you if there's jam nearby that wants to get eaten at that very moment.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有iPhone应用程序能实时告诉你附近哪里有果酱正等着被吃掉。

sentences.en: I mean, what can you do?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这能怎么办呢？

sentences.en: Aziz has co-written a book with the sociologist Eric Kleinenberg.
sentences.zh: 阿齐兹与社会学家埃里克·克莱嫩伯格合著了一本书。

sentences.en: It's called Modern Romance.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《现代浪漫》。

sentences.en: We taped a live conversation at George Washington University's Listener Auditorium,
sentences.zh: 我们在乔治华盛顿大学的利斯纳礼堂录制了一场现场对话，

sentences.en: and we played an excerpt for you in the fall.
sentences.zh: 并在秋季为您播放了节选。

sentences.en: We are working on new podcasts this week, and we thought you might enjoy this encore presentation.
sentences.zh: 本周我们正在制作新的播客，觉得您可能会喜欢这次重播。

sentences.en: If you know anything about Aziz, we don't need to tell you, this episode is going to be a little racy.
sentences.zh: 如果你了解阿齐兹，就不用我多说了，这期节目会有点劲爆。

sentences.en: If you're in the car with kids, you might want to save it for later.
sentences.zh: 如果你正带着孩子开车，可能想留到以后再听。

sentences.en: I want to jump to one particular section that you start right at the top of the book,
sentences.zh: 我想跳到书开头的一个特定章节，

sentences.en: looking at ways in which people text one another.
sentences.zh: 探讨人们互相发短信的方式。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And the fact that people turn out to be surprisingly bad at texting.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们在发短信方面表现得令人惊讶地糟糕。

sentences.en: Actually, I should correct that.
sentences.zh: 其实，我应该更正一下。

sentences.en: What you're saying is that men turn out to be surprisingly bad at texting women.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，男性在给女性发短信方面表现得令人惊讶地糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, I will say this, okay?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我得这么说，好吗？

sentences.en: When we, like, asked women, like, well, what are the things you like when guys text you?
sentences.zh: 当我们问女性，你们喜欢男生发什么样的短信时，

sentences.en: Like, what are the factors that make a text that you like?
sentences.zh: 比如，什么样的因素会让你们喜欢一条短信？

sentences.en: And kind of the consensus we got was asking them to do a specific thing at a specific time,
sentences.zh: 我们得到的共识是，要明确提出在特定时间做某件具体的事，

sentences.en: saying something that maybe, like, recalled, like, an interaction that they had in the past
sentences.zh: 或者提到一些过去共同经历的互动，

sentences.en: to kind of just show that you were engaged and this was something that you were into.
sentences.zh: 以此来表明你很投入，并且对此很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And the last thing was, like, just, you know, some sort of humor is also helpful.
sentences.zh: 最后一点是，你知道，带点幽默感也很有帮助。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the book, we talk about this stuff,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在书里我们讨论过这些，

sentences.en: and it's not from the perspective of this is what you should do.
sentences.zh: 并不是从“你应该怎么做”的角度出发。

sentences.en: More like, how the f*** do people not know, like, this is all you have to do?
sentences.zh: 更像是，他妈的这些人怎么会不知道，这不就是你唯一需要做的吗？

sentences.en: Like, the bar is startlingly low.
sentences.zh: 门槛低得惊人。

sentences.en: Like, it's really, like, very scary how low the bar is.
sentences.zh: 门槛低到令人害怕，真的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether we can have you just read a short excerpt from the book
sentences.zh: 我想让你读一下书中的一小段，

sentences.en: that talks about how badly men are doing this.
sentences.zh: 谈谈男性在这方面做得有多差。

sentences.en: And you have a little excerpt here with a guy who tries to text a woman.
sentences.zh: 你这里有个小片段，讲的是一个男人试图给女人发短信。

sentences.en: It's on page 42 for anyone of you who want to read along.
sentences.zh: 在第42页，想跟着读的朋友可以翻一下。

sentences.en: Okay, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Some people say it doesn't matter what you text someone.
sentences.zh: 有些人说给别人发什么内容不重要。

sentences.en: If they like you, they like you.
sentences.zh: 如果他们喜欢你，他们就是喜欢你。

sentences.en: After interviewing hundreds of singles,
sentences.zh: 在采访了数百名单身人士后，

sentences.en: I can scientifically confirm that this is total bulls***.
sentences.zh: 我可以科学地证实，这纯属胡扯。

sentences.en: For those who doubt me, here's an example from a show I did
sentences.zh: 对于那些怀疑我的人，这里有一个我在2014年春天

sentences.en: at the Chicago Theater in the spring of 2014.
sentences.zh: 在芝加哥剧院演出时的例子。

sentences.en: During that tour, after material about texting,
sentences.zh: 在那次巡演中，讲完关于发短信的段子后，

sentences.en: I would ask if anyone in the audience had recently met someone
sentences.zh: 我会问观众里有没有人最近刚认识某人，

sentences.en: and had been texting back and forth.
sentences.zh: 并且一直在互发短信。

sentences.en: If they had, they would come onto the stage,
sentences.zh: 如果有，他们会上台，

sentences.en: and I would pick a few people and read, analyze,
sentences.zh: 我会挑选几个人，阅读、分析，

sentences.en: and ask them about what was happening in their messages.
sentences.zh: 并询问他们短信里发生了什么。

sentences.en: At this particular show, I was speaking with Rachel,
sentences.zh: 在这一场演出中，我与瑞秋交谈，

sentences.en: who had met a guy at a good friend's wedding.
sentences.zh: 她在一位好友的婚礼上认识了一个男人。

sentences.en: As it happened, the guy was also a friend of her sister's,
sentences.zh: 巧的是，那个人也是她姐姐的朋友，

sentences.en: so he had a pretty good shot at a first date with her.
sentences.zh: 所以他很有机会和她约会。

sentences.en: She was single.
sentences.zh: 她是单身。

sentences.en: She was interested.
sentences.zh: 她也有兴趣。

sentences.en: All he had to do was send her a simple message,
sentences.zh: 他只需要发一条简单的消息，

sentences.en: introducing himself and asking her to do something.
sentences.zh: 介绍一下自己，约她做点什么。

sentences.en: Here's what happened.
sentences.zh: 结果发生了什么呢？

sentences.en: He sends his first message.
sentences.zh: 他发出了第一条消息。

sentences.en: Hi, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 嗨，瑞秋。

sentences.en: Since I never got a chance to ask you to dance at Marissa and Chris's wedding,
sentences.zh: 因为在玛丽莎和克里斯的婚礼上我没机会请你跳舞，

sentences.en: I'm Chris's old roommate from Purdue.
sentences.zh: 我是克里斯在普渡大学的老室友。

sentences.en: He and your sister gave me your number.
sentences.zh: 他和你的姐姐给了我你的号码。

sentences.en: I wanted to say hi and sort of texty introduce myself.
sentences.zh: 我想打个招呼，顺便发短信自我介绍一下。

sentences.en: Haha.
sentences.zh: 哈哈。

sentences.en: Hope you had a great weekend.
sentences.zh: 希望你周末过得愉快。

sentences.en: Dot, dot, dot.
sentences.zh: 点，点，点。

sentences.en: Hope to chat with you soon.
sentences.zh: 希望能很快和你聊天。

sentences.en: Rachel wrote back ten minutes later.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋十分钟后回信了。

sentences.en: Hey, great to meet you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Currently enjoying my birthday weekend with lots of good Mexican food.
sentences.zh: 我正在享受我的生日周末，吃了很多美味的墨西哥菜。

sentences.en: It happens when your birthday is in Cinco de Mayo.
sentences.zh: 生日在五月五日节就是这样。

sentences.en: Hope you had a great weekend, too.
sentences.zh: 也希望你周末过得愉快。

sentences.en: He wrote back shortly.
sentences.zh: 他很快回信了。

sentences.en: I totally realized upon reading my last message,
sentences.zh: 读完上一条消息我才意识到，

sentences.en: I didn't include my name.
sentences.zh: 我没写名字。

sentences.en: Haha.
sentences.zh: 哈哈。

sentences.en: I'm Will.
sentences.zh: 我是威尔。

sentences.en: Smiley face.
sentences.zh: 笑脸。

sentences.en: Feliz cumpleaños as well.
sentences.zh: 也祝你生日快乐。

sentences.en: And totally digging on the Cinco de Mayo theme.
sentences.zh: 而且非常喜欢五月五日节这个主题。

sentences.en: Rachel never met Will.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋再也没见过威尔。

sentences.en: After a few messages of this nature, Rachel stopped responding.
sentences.zh: 在几条这样的消息之后，瑞秋停止了回复。

sentences.en: None of us know Will.
sentences.zh: 我们都不认识威尔。

sentences.en: You may be a kind, handsome man with a heart of gold.
sentences.zh: 你可能是一个善良、英俊、心地纯良的男人。

sentences.en: But all we have to go on is those messages.
sentences.zh: 但我们只能通过那些短信来判断。

sentences.en: And those messages have shaped in our minds
sentences.zh: 而那些短信在我们脑海中塑造了一个

sentences.en: a very dorky, terrifyingly Caucasian weirdo.
sentences.zh: 非常书呆子气、令人毛骨悚然的白人怪胎形象。

sentences.en: So, one of the things that you point out in the book
sentences.zh: 所以，你在书中指出的其中一点是，

sentences.en: is that there's this arms race in waiting when someone texts you.
sentences.zh: 当有人给你发短信时，存在一种“等待军备竞赛”。

sentences.en: That if you respond to a text right away,
sentences.zh: 如果你立刻回复短信，

sentences.en: you instantly lose all leverage
sentences.zh: 你瞬间就失去了所有筹码，

sentences.en: because you indicate interest, you indicate desperation.
sentences.zh: 因为你表现出了兴趣，表现出了绝望。

sentences.en: So, you wait when someone texts you.
sentences.zh: 所以，当别人给你发短信时，你会等待。

sentences.en: And now that person is playing the same game with you.
sentences.zh: 现在那个人也在和你玩同样的游戏。

sentences.en: So, they wait and respond to texting you.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们也在等待回复你的短信。

sentences.en: And now you have this extended waiting game.
sentences.zh: 现在你们陷入了一场漫长的等待游戏。

sentences.en: It's so weird.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: And it's weird because everyone knows what people are doing
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，每个人都知道对方在干什么，

sentences.en: and they still f***ing do it.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是他妈的照做不误。

sentences.en: Like, oh, you're going to wait 20 minutes?
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，你要等20分钟？

sentences.en: Oh, did you have a meeting?
sentences.zh: 哦，你在开会吗？

sentences.en: No, you f***ing didn't.
sentences.zh: 不，你他妈根本没在开会。

sentences.en: You were waiting on purpose.
sentences.zh: 你是故意在等。

sentences.en: Well, guess what?
sentences.zh: 好吧，猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I'm going to wait 40 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我要等40分钟。

sentences.en: I'm going to double that s***
sentences.zh: 我要把这破事加倍，

sentences.en: because I have s*** going on too.
sentences.zh: 因为我也有很多破事要忙。

sentences.en: Not really, but I'm going to pretend like I do.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有，但我会假装我很忙。

sentences.en: It's so weird.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: You know, that was the thing that was interesting to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那件事让我觉得很有趣。

sentences.en: Like, I wondered, like, why did that waiting drive me crazy
sentences.zh: 比如，我纳闷，为什么当我单身时，

sentences.en: when I was single and, like, had to deal with that?
sentences.zh: 不得不处理这种等待时，它会让我发疯？

sentences.en: Like, I would go crazy.
sentences.zh: 我会发疯的。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the book, we looked at a lot of studies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在书里，我们研究了很多案例。

sentences.en: We talked to a lot of very smart people.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了很多非常聪明的人。

sentences.en: And they explained it to me and it made sense.
sentences.zh: 他们向我解释了原因，这说得通。

sentences.en: Like, basically, the idea is, like, let's say you're a guy.
sentences.zh: 基本上，想法是这样的，假设你是个男人。

sentences.en: You meet three women and you text all three of them.
sentences.zh: 你认识了三个女人，给她们三个人都发了短信。

sentences.en: And two of them write you back.
sentences.zh: 其中两个给你回了信。

sentences.en: The two that write you back, they kind of put your mind at ease, right?
sentences.zh: 回信的那两个让你感到安心，对吧？

sentences.en: But the third one has not written you back.
sentences.zh: 但第三个没有回信。

sentences.en: So they're not putting your mind at ease.
sentences.zh: 所以她们没让你感到安心。

sentences.en: And they've created uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 她们制造了不确定性。

sentences.en: And uncertainty is very powerful and it sticks in your mind.
sentences.zh: 而不确定性是非常强大的，它会萦绕在你的脑海里。

sentences.en: And you're like, well, what s*** is going on?
sentences.zh: 你会想，到底发生了什么破事？

sentences.en: What did I do?
sentences.zh: 我做了什么？

sentences.en: Did I do something wrong?
sentences.zh: 我做错什么了吗？

sentences.en: Did this person not like me?
sentences.zh: 这个人不喜欢我吗？

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: And so that person has more presence in your mind.
sentences.zh: 所以那个人在你的脑海中占据了更多空间。

sentences.en: And just that presence on your mind can sometimes develop into attraction.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是这种萦绕在心头的感觉，有时就能演变成吸引力。

sentences.en: So when they finally do put your mind at ease, it's more meaningful to you.
sentences.zh: 所以当她们最终让你安心时，这对你来说更有意义。

sentences.en: But there's also kind of, like, at a certain point,
sentences.zh: 但也有某种程度，比如在某个节点，

sentences.en: if you wait too long, then the person's like, well, screw this person.
sentences.zh: 如果你等得太久，对方就会想，去他妈的这个人。

sentences.en: Like, they waited too long.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们等得太久了。

sentences.en: Like, screw them.
sentences.zh: 去他妈的。

sentences.en: I'm going to hang out with one of these other people that wrote me back quickly or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我要去和那些回信快的人出去玩了。

sentences.en: So it's never quite a precise thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这从来都不是一个精确的事情。

sentences.en: There's not, like, something you can say where it's like, okay,
sentences.zh: 没有什么话可以说，比如，好吧，

sentences.en: if you wait, like, this amount of minutes, you're going to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 如果你等，比如，这么几分钟，你就完美了。

sentences.en: Like, all those things vary from person to person.
sentences.zh: 这些事情因人而异。

sentences.en: There's a lot of factors.
sentences.zh: 有很多因素。

sentences.en: But the thing we learned is, like, that amount of time decreases as you get to younger people.
sentences.zh: 但我们了解到的是，随着年龄的增长，这段等待时间会缩短。

sentences.en: Like, I'm 32.
sentences.zh: 比如，我今年32岁。

sentences.en: If you talk to someone my age, they're like, oh, if they wait, like, you know, a day or, like, six hours,
sentences.zh: 如果你和像我这个年纪的人聊天，他们会说，哦，如果他们等，你知道，一天或者，比如，六个小时，

sentences.en: it's a little unnerving.
sentences.zh: 这会让人有点不安。

sentences.en: If you talk to someone who's, like, in college now, they're like,
sentences.zh: 如果你和现在上大学的人聊天，他们会说，

sentences.en: I haven't heard anything in five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我五分钟没收到消息了。

sentences.en: What's happened?
sentences.zh: 发生什么事了？

sentences.en: That window is getting smaller and smaller.
sentences.zh: 那个窗口期正变得越来越小。

sentences.en: When we come back, we'll talk about how the ever-growing pool of dating options can be both a blessing and a curse.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论不断增长的约会选择池如何既是福也是祸。

sentences.en: This is related to an idea in psychology known as the paradox of choice.
sentences.zh: 这与心理学中一个被称为“选择悖论”的概念有关。

sentences.en: Having too many choices can be tough when you're dating or when you're buying jam.
sentences.zh: 当你约会或买果酱时，选择太多可能会很麻烦。

sentences.en: You know, you go on a date and you go to the bathroom, like, a few pieces of jam have texted you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你去约会，然后去上个厕所，就有几位“果酱”给你发了短信。

sentences.en: You're like, what the f*** is this?
sentences.zh: 你会想，这到底是什么鬼？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Welcome back to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: Aziz Ansari talks in his book about the vast number of dating choices people have today.
sentences.zh: 阿齐兹·安萨里（Aziz Ansari）在他的书中谈到了当今人们拥有的大量约会选择。

sentences.en: This led to an idea that's been explored in the social sciences.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一个在社会科学中被探讨过的观点。

sentences.en: It's known as the paradox of choice.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“选择悖论”。

sentences.en: One of the big changes for people that are, like, dating now is you have more options than any generation of people ever.
sentences.zh: 对于现在约会的人来说，最大的变化之一就是你拥有的选择比历史上任何一代人都多。

sentences.en: You know, when we talked to people that were living in retirement homes and stuff, it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们和住在养老院之类地方的人交谈时，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: They talked about how, like, especially to women, it was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了，比如，特别是对女性而言，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, they were saying, like, well, you know, I was 20 years old, I was living with my parents, I didn't have the opportunity to pursue education or my own career,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会说，嗯，你知道，我20岁的时候，和父母住在一起，没有机会去追求教育或我自己的事业，

sentences.en: I didn't really get to become an adult until I got married.
sentences.zh: 直到结婚我才真正成为一个成年人。

sentences.en: And there was some guy that lived in the neighborhood, he was pretty nice, and I wanted to get out of the house, and I was like, all right, I'll get married, you know.
sentences.zh: 附近住着个男人，人挺好的，我想搬出去住，我就想，好吧，那我就结婚吧，你知道。

sentences.en: And they really said that.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是这么说的。

sentences.en: I was like, it sounds like it, because they were like, some of the women, they were really happy, they were like, oh, we grew to have this deep bond.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，听起来确实如此，因为他们，有些女性，她们真的很幸福，她们说，哦，我们逐渐建立了这种深厚的纽带。

sentences.en: But other women were like, no, not as much of a bond.
sentences.zh: 但其他女性则说，不，纽带没那么深。

sentences.en: And getting married was kind of the first step in adulthood for those generations.
sentences.zh: 对那些世代的人来说，结婚算是成年后的第一步。

sentences.en: But for us, this, you know, people now, marriage isn't always a first step.
sentences.zh: 但对我们，你知道，现在的人来说，婚姻并不总是第一步。

sentences.en: You know, you go to college, you pursue a career, you live in a bunch of different places, and you meet so many people throughout all these different stages of your life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你上大学，追求事业，住在许多不同的地方，在人生的各个阶段会遇到很多人。

sentences.en: You have this whole stage of life that is referred to as emerging adulthood, and, yeah, you meet so many people that way, and then you add in the online dating aspect of things,
sentences.zh: 你经历了被称为“成年初期”的整个阶段，是的，你通过这种方式遇到了很多人，然后再加上在线约会这一面，

sentences.en: and you have more options than anyone could have possibly imagined in those generations of retirement homes.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的选择比那些养老院世代的人所能想象的要多得多。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I can see why a dating pool of three people is too small to actually find your life partner.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我能理解为什么只有三个人的约会池太小，无法真正找到你的终身伴侣。

sentences.en: But a dating pool of 30,000 or 300,000 is just unmanageable, because what happens is every time you meet someone who's potentially interesting,
sentences.zh: 但一个拥有3万或30万人的约会池简直无法管理，因为每当你遇到一个潜在的有趣的人时，

sentences.en: a little voice in the back of your head says, if you wait for another two days, you could find someone better than this.
sentences.zh: 你脑海深处的一个小声音就会说，如果你再等两天，你可能会找到比这更好的人。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, well, the problem is, it's what we refer to, this gentleman, Barry Schwartz, that we interviewed in the book, he does a lot of research on choice,
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，问题在于，这就是我们所说的，这位绅士，巴里·施瓦茨（Barry Schwartz），我们在书中采访过他，他做了很多关于选择的研究，

sentences.en: and he wrote this book called The Paradox of Choice, and kind of the main thesis of that book is the idea that, like, you know, when you have more options, your instinct is, oh,
sentences.zh: 他写了一本名为《选择悖论》的书，那本书的主要论点是，你知道，当你拥有更多选择时，你的本能是，哦，

sentences.en: well, that's better.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那更好。

sentences.en: I have more options, I have more things to choose from, I'll be happier.
sentences.zh: 我有更多选择，我有更多东西可以挑选，我会更快乐。

sentences.en: But in reality, when they do study after study, they find the more options you have, the harder it is to make a decision, and when you do make a decision,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当他们进行一项又一项研究时，他们发现选择越多，就越难做决定，而当你真正做出决定时，

sentences.en: you end up being less satisfied, because you're thinking about whether you made the wrong decision, or whether one of these other things would have been a better match for you.
sentences.zh: 你最终会感到不那么满足，因为你会思考自己是否做出了错误的决定，或者其他选择是否更适合你。

sentences.en: And then the really famous study is this study they did in a grocery store, where they had two different displays with jams, and one display had, like, you know, five jams,
sentences.zh: 还有一个非常著名的研究是在杂货店做的，他们有两个不同的果酱展示台，一个展示台有，比如，你知道，五种果酱，

sentences.en: and then the other display had, like, 36 jaMs.
sentences.zh: 而另一个展示台有，比如，36种果酱。

sentences.en: And whenever it was the five jams, people were way more likely to buy the jams, and when they had the 36 jams, they were just overwhelmed, and they didn't know what to do,
sentences.zh: 每当是五种果酱时，人们购买果酱的可能性要大得多，而当他们有36种果酱时，他们只是感到不知所措，不知道该怎么办，

sentences.en: and they ended up not buying jams sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时他们最终根本不买果酱。

sentences.en: So, and they also said this, which is really interesting, they said, like, oh, people that bought the jams from the 36, like, the bigger display, whatever else,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们还说了这一点，这非常有趣，他们说，比如，哦，从36种，比如，更大的展示台购买果酱的人，无论如何，

sentences.en: I'm getting these numbers wrong, I'm paraphrasing, but the core of the thing is right.
sentences.zh: 我的数字可能记错了，我是在转述，但核心内容是对的。

sentences.en: When they bought from the one with the bigger display with more options, the people reported being less satisfied with the jam, which I found really hilarious.
sentences.zh: 当他们从那个拥有更多选择的更大展示台购买时，人们报告说对果酱的满意度较低，我觉得这真的很滑稽。

sentences.en: The idea that someone ate jam, like, this jam's not satisfying, what's wrong with this jam, this doesn't taste like strawberries.
sentences.zh: 有人吃了果酱，觉得“这果酱不令人满意，这果酱怎么了，这尝起来不像草莓”的想法。

sentences.en: But the thing we say in the book is, like, to me, like, that totally applies to modern romance, because, I mean, like, there's just too much goddamn jam out there.
sentences.zh: 但我们在书中说的是，对我来说，这完全适用于现代浪漫，因为，我的意思是，外面有太多该死的“果酱”了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, you go on a date, and you go to the bathroom, like, a few pieces of jam have texted you, and you're like, what the f*** is this?
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，你去约会，然后去上个厕所，就有几位“果酱”给你发了短信，你会想，这到底是什么鬼？

sentences.en: It's, you go online, there's so much jam out there.
sentences.zh: 就是，你上网，外面有太多的“果酱”了。

sentences.en: There's iPhone apps that literally tell you if there's jam nearby that wants to get eaten at that very moment.
sentences.zh: 有iPhone应用程序会直接告诉你，此时此刻附近是否有想被“吃掉”的“果酱”。

sentences.en: I mean, what can you do?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你能做什么？

sentences.en: You know, you talk in the book about this guy you interviewed, who I think was on Match.com, and you actually got to observe him making choices,
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在书中谈到了你采访的那个家伙，我想他是在Match.com上，你实际上观察了他做选择的过程，

sentences.en: where he was sort of reviewing pictures of women, and then deciding whether he liked them or not.
sentences.zh: 他当时在浏览女性的照片，然后决定他是否喜欢她们。

sentences.en: And I don't know if you remember the specific anecdote, but I'm wondering if you can just tell us about it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否还记得那个具体的轶事，但我很想让你给我们讲讲。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember this guy.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得这个人。

sentences.en: So, he just, he didn't seem like a, like, he wasn't like a hunk or anything, like, he wasn't a stud.
sentences.zh: 所以，他看起来不像，比如，他不是什么大帅哥，比如，他不是那种万人迷。

sentences.en: He was just kind of like, and this is mean, but he was just kind of like a mediocre white guy.
sentences.zh: 他只是有点像，这话有点刻薄，但他只是那种平庸的白人男性。

sentences.en: And he logged on to his account, and it said, like, oh, he was a Match.com account in this case.
sentences.zh: 他登录了他的账户，上面显示，比如，哦，在这个案例中他是一个Match.com账户。

sentences.en: And he looks on it, and he was just like, and it said, like, you have these mini matches.
sentences.zh: 他看着它，他只是，上面显示，比如，你有这些匹配对象。

sentences.en: And I looked at the photo, and I was like, wow, that woman's very attractive.
sentences.zh: 我看了照片，我当时想，哇，那个女人非常有吸引力。

sentences.en: And then he looked at her profile, and he was, like, debating whether he should send her a message.
sentences.zh: 然后他看了她的个人资料，他在纠结是否应该给她发信息。

sentences.en: He was like, no.
sentences.zh: 他说，不。

sentences.en: And I was like, what?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，什么？

sentences.en: Why are you not sending her a message?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不给她发信息？

sentences.en: And he was like, mm, she likes the Red Sox.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，她喜欢红袜队（Red Sox）。

sentences.en: And I was like, what?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，什么？

sentences.en: And then, like, I saw him go to another woman and ignore her, and then he ignored, like, one other woman,
sentences.zh: 然后，比如，我看到他转而去看另一个女人并忽略了她，然后他又忽略了，比如，另外一个女人，

sentences.en: and then he sent this other woman, like, a quick message.
sentences.zh: 然后他给另一个女人发了一条简短的信息。

sentences.en: And it blew my mind.
sentences.zh: 这让我大开眼界。

sentences.en: Because if any of those other three women that he, like, put an X on,
sentences.zh: 因为如果他打叉的那三个女人中的任何一个，

sentences.en: if they had seen him in a bar, like, you know, 20 years ago and, like, smiled at him,
sentences.zh: 如果她们在酒吧里见到他，比如，你知道，20年前，然后，比如，对他微笑，

sentences.en: he would have, he would have went crazy.
sentences.zh: 他会，他会欣喜若狂的。

sentences.en: He would have went crazy.
sentences.zh: 他会欣喜若狂的。

sentences.en: And seemed like intelligent, thoughtful people, just, you know, based on what little I saw from the profile,
sentences.zh: 而且看起来是聪明、体贴的人，只是，你知道，基于我从个人资料中看到的那么一点点信息，

sentences.en: but they seemed like interesting people where it would be a catch for this guy.
sentences.zh: 但她们看起来是有趣的人，对这个家伙来说会是很好的伴侣。

sentences.en: But now, he was just like, meh, whatever.
sentences.zh: 但现在，他只是说，嗯，随便吧。

sentences.en: Like, there's so many people out here.
sentences.zh: 比如，外面有这么多人。

sentences.en: Who cares?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: So, but here's the thing that I find really sad about what you're describing,
sentences.zh: 所以，但这就是我觉得你所描述的事情中非常可悲的一点，

sentences.en: which is that people are looking at these pictures,
sentences.zh: 那就是人们在看这些照片，

sentences.en: and they're making judgments about this other person based on this very, very small amount of information.
sentences.zh: 并且基于这些非常、非常少的信息对另一个人做出判断。

sentences.en: And often based on things that they think are important criteria to them.
sentences.zh: 而且通常是基于他们认为对自己重要的标准。

sentences.en: So, if you ask people, they will tell you, I want someone who's this tall or this short or this color hair or this body profile and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你问人们，他们会告诉你，我想要一个多高或多矮，或者什么发色，或者什么身材等等的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But if you actually look at the data of who people end up with,
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的看看人们最终和谁在一起的数据，

sentences.en: people often don't end up with the people that they say they're actually looking for.
sentences.zh: 人们往往最终并没有和他们口中所说的那种人在一起。

sentences.en: So, if they eliminate people based on the criteria they think they have, they might be eliminating their soulmates.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们基于自己认为拥有的标准去淘汰人，他们可能正在淘汰他们的灵魂伴侣。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, there's plenty of studies that show that we're horrible at knowing what we really like, you know.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，有很多研究表明我们根本不知道自己真正喜欢什么，你知道。

sentences.en: Whenever they look at these online sites and they see what people say they prefer and what they actually go after,
sentences.zh: 每当他们查看这些在线网站，看到人们说他们偏好什么，以及他们实际上追求什么时，

sentences.en: it's always, there's always a big contrast of like, what?
sentences.zh: 总是，总是有一个巨大的反差，比如，什么？

sentences.en: You said you didn't like this, but that's actually what you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 你说你不喜欢这个，但那实际上正是你感兴趣的。

sentences.en: And I think that goes back to this idea of like, you know, all these online dating sites, you have all these filters and all this stuff,
sentences.zh: 我认为这又回到了这个想法，比如，你知道，所有这些在线约会网站，你有所有的过滤器和所有这些东西，

sentences.en: but none of it really matters.
sentences.zh: 但这些其实都不重要。

sentences.en: Like, it's really just about like this connection that you have with someone in person and seeing if there's some sort of spark or connection.
sentences.zh: 比如，这真的只是关于你和某人面对面时的那种联系，看看是否有某种火花或连接。

sentences.en: Like, when you have this connection with someone in real life, you don't stop and go, wait, wait, wait, hold on.
sentences.zh: 比如，当你在现实生活中与某人有这种联系时，你不会停下来，说，等等，等等，等等，等一下。

sentences.en: But what are your favorite movies?
sentences.zh: 但你最喜欢的电影是什么？

sentences.en: Like, you're just, you don't give a shit.
sentences.zh: 比如，你只是，你根本不在乎。

sentences.en: You're engaged with the person and you like it and it's fun.
sentences.zh: 你和那个人相处得很融洽，你喜欢它，这很有趣。

sentences.en: And I think sometimes with these online sites, the people that seem to be a little frustrated were people that were trying to find this perfect person
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有时在这些在线网站上，那些看起来有点沮丧的人是那些试图找到完美伴侣的人，

sentences.en: and spending this extended period of time, like messaging back and forth and trying to find this elusive rapport.
sentences.zh: 并花费了很长一段时间，比如来回发信息，试图找到那种难以捉摸的默契。

sentences.en: And really, you just find that in person.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，你只能在面对面时找到它。

sentences.en: And I think our kind of big takeaway from online dating was what this woman, Helen Fisher, told us.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从在线约会中得到的最大收获是海伦·费舍尔（Helen Fisher）告诉我们的。

sentences.en: And she's like this amazingly smart social anthropologist and also works with Match.com.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常聪明的社会人类学家，也与Match.com合作。

sentences.en: And she's like, you know, these sites shouldn't be called online dating sites.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，这些网站不应该被称为在线约会网站。

sentences.en: They should be called online introduction services because you want to meet this person in person.
sentences.zh: 它们应该被称为在线介绍服务，因为你想面对面地见到这个人。

sentences.en: Like, and what I realized is like, you know, you don't meet the perfect person online.
sentences.zh: 比如，我意识到的是，比如，你知道，你不会在网上遇到完美的人。

sentences.en: You can meet a person online, but to find out they're perfect, you have to see how you are in person.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上遇到一个人，但要发现他们是否完美，你必须看看你们面对面时是什么样子。

sentences.en: So in other words, you really, you have to get to sort of date three before you actually figure out whether this person is for you or not.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你真的，你必须进行到第三次约会左右，才能真正弄清楚这个人是否适合你。

sentences.en: But if you're in constantly swipe right, swipe left mode, you're not going to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 但如果你一直处于向右滑、向左滑的模式，你就无法达到那个点。

sentences.en: Or even worse than the swipe right, swipe left mode is this mode of like, oh, let me just keep sending messages and see if this is my dream person.
sentences.zh: 或者比向右滑、向左滑模式更糟糕的是这种模式，比如，哦，让我继续发送信息，看看这是否是我的梦中情人。

sentences.en: You know, Tinder actually think, and those kind of swipe apps, I totally see why those came about.
sentences.zh: 你知道，Tinder实际上认为，以及那些类似的滑动应用程序，我完全明白它们为什么会出现。

sentences.en: Like, there's some people that would say, oh, well, that seems really shallow, just to see a picture and just like swipe it and decide if you're going to meet someone.
sentences.zh: 比如，有些人会说，哦，嗯，这看起来真的很肤浅，仅仅看一张照片就滑动它，决定是否要见某人。

sentences.en: But I mean, when you go into a bar or a party, you're looking at people and going, no, no, yes, you're doing that.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，当你走进酒吧或聚会时，你也在看着人们，然后说，不，不，是的，你就是在做那个。

sentences.en: So I'm trying to internalize your lesson,
sentences.zh: 所以我正在努力内化你的教训，

sentences.en: which is that it's less important to meet new people and more important to spend time with the people you meet to figure out if they're actually right for you.
sentences.zh: 那就是认识新的人并不重要，重要的是花时间和那些你遇到的人相处，以弄清楚他们是否真的适合你。

sentences.en: So the thing we mention in the book is what we call the the flow rider theory of acquired likability through repetition, which which basically which basically is saying, like, yes,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在书中提到的事情就是我们所说的“通过重复获得喜爱度的弗洛·里达（Flo Rida）理论”，这基本上是说，是的，

sentences.en: there are people.
sentences.zh: 确实有这样的人。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: But I'd like to think there's a lot of great people out there and a lot of people that were quick to dismiss.
sentences.zh: 但我愿意认为外面有很多很棒的人，也有很多我们很快就否定的人。

sentences.en: If you apply this theory, the theory is basically like we're all like a flow rider song, you know, the first time you hear us, you're like, all right, flow rider.
sentences.zh: 如果你应用这个理论，这个理论基本上就像我们都是一首弗洛·里达的歌，你知道，你第一次听到我们时，你会想，好吧，弗洛·里达。

sentences.en: I've heard this before.
sentences.zh: 我以前听过这个。

sentences.en: Get it out of here.
sentences.zh: 把它拿走。

sentences.en: Leave me alone.
sentences.zh: 别管我。

sentences.en: And then you keep hearing it and it gets stuck in your head.
sentences.zh: 然后你一直听它，它就会萦绕在你的脑海里。

sentences.en: You're like, flow rider, you've done it again.
sentences.zh: 你会想，弗洛·里达，你又做到了。

sentences.en: Let's dance.
sentences.zh: 让我们跳舞吧。

sentences.en: I was reading a section of the book this afternoon that brought back some memories from some years ago involving a certain congressman from New York.
sentences.zh: 今天下午我正在读这本书的一个章节，它勾起了几年前涉及纽约某位国会议员的一些回忆。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And some Facebook messages he had exchanged with a woman named Lisa from Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 还有他与一位名叫丽莎（Lisa）的拉斯维加斯女性交换的一些Facebook信息。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you might be able to read this exchange for us.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能为我们读一下这段对话。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And I want to ask you whether you think these online sites and this technology has increased the risk of indiscretions and infidelity.
sentences.zh: 我想问你，你是否认为这些在线网站和这项技术增加了轻率行为和不忠的风险。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I remember reading the Anthony Weiner Facebook messages, seeing the way he was just messaging random women all over the country
sentences.zh: 我记得读过安东尼·韦纳（Anthony Weiner）的Facebook信息，看到他给全国各地的随机女性发信息的方式，

sentences.en: and watching the messages quickly escalate from innocuous to very sexual was unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 看着这些信息迅速从无害升级到非常色情，真是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: This is a transcript of a chat session he had with one of these women, a lady named Lisa from Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 这是他与其中一位女性，一位名叫丽莎的拉斯维加斯女士的聊天记录。

sentences.en: Weiner and Lisa.
sentences.zh: 韦纳和丽莎。

sentences.en: Lisa, sorry to bring this back, guys, but it is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，抱歉把这个话题带回来，伙计们，但它确实很迷人。

sentences.en: Lisa, I'm trying to find the wonderful Anthony Weiner who I fell in love with for yelling at those damn Republicans the other day.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，我正在努力寻找那位美妙的安东尼·韦纳，因为他前几天对那些该死的共和党人咆哮，我爱上了他。

sentences.en: And you were as funny as hell on The Daily Show.
sentences.zh: 而且你在《每日秀》（The Daily Show）上表现得非常有趣。

sentences.en: Your friend requests are full.
sentences.zh: 你的好友请求已满。

sentences.en: You must friend me.
sentences.zh: 你一定要加我好友。

sentences.en: Anthony, you were awesome.
sentences.zh: 安东尼，你太棒了。

sentences.en: Anthony, thank you, Lisa.
sentences.zh: 安东尼，谢谢你，丽莎。

sentences.en: Glad you have my back.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你支持我。

sentences.en: You keeping an eye on that wackadoodle Sharon Angle for us?
sentences.zh: 你有没有帮我们盯着那个怪胎莎伦·安格尔？

sentences.en: Lisa, how insane is she?
sentences.zh: 丽莎，她到底有多疯狂？

sentences.en: Who needs Social Security, Medicare, or education?
sentences.zh: 谁还需要社会保障、医疗保险或教育呢？

sentences.en: If this wacko wins my state, I swear I'll have to move.
sentences.zh: 如果这个怪胎赢了我所在的州，我发誓我一定要搬走。

sentences.en: She may be dumber than plain, and that is tough to find.
sentences.zh: 她可能比白痴还蠢，这可真不容易。

sentences.en: Like this cute new pic of you, when are you coming to Vegas to help me beat up the right-wing crazies?
sentences.zh: 喜欢你这张可爱的新照片，你什么时候来拉斯维加斯帮我教训那些右翼疯子？

sentences.en: Anthony, this is my pull-my-finger shot.
sentences.zh: 安东尼，这是我的“快来撩我”照。

sentences.en: Glad you like.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你喜欢。

sentences.en: I'm ready for a Vegas trip.
sentences.zh: 我准备好去拉斯维加斯了。

sentences.en: Truth-telling during the day?
sentences.zh: 白天讲真话？

sentences.en: Got a night plan for us?
sentences.zh: 晚上有什么计划吗？

sentences.en: Question mark.
sentences.zh: 问号。

sentences.en: Lisa, ha-ha, that was a very loaded question.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，哈哈，这问题可真是意有所指啊。

sentences.en: I've got all kinds of night plans for us.
sentences.zh: 我为我们准备了各种各样的夜间计划。

sentences.en: When are you coming?
sentences.zh: 你什么时候来？

sentences.en: Anthony, don't know.
sentences.zh: 安东尼，不知道。

sentences.en: Make me an offer I can't refuse.
sentences.zh: 给我一个我无法拒绝的提议吧。

sentences.en: Lisa, to get us in the mood, first we watch back-to-back episodes of The Daily Show and Colbert Report.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，为了调动气氛，我们先连看几集《每日秀》和《科尔伯特报告》。

sentences.en: Then, to really spice things up, we go to face all of my neighbors sharing Angle yard signs.
sentences.zh: 然后，为了增加点情趣，我们去面对那些在院子里插着安格尔竞选标语的邻居们。

sentences.en: Then, when we are really hot, we go to the bookstore and cover all of the Glenn Beck books with copies of The Audacity of Hope.
sentences.zh: 接着，当我们兴致正浓时，我们去书店，把格伦·贝克的书全部用《无畏的希望》覆盖住。

sentences.en: I do this about once a week.
sentences.zh: 我每周大概做一次这个。

sentences.en: You can tell I'm a very exciting girl.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出我是一个非常刺激的女孩。

sentences.en: Or, if this is not your thing, we can just get drunk and have mad, passionate sex.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果你不喜欢这些，我们可以直接喝醉，然后疯狂地做爱。

sentences.en: For me, the most offensive part was that he used the word whack-a-doodle.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最冒犯的部分是他用了“怪胎”这个词。

sentences.en: Also, did you catch that sly, almost subliminal blink-and-you-might-miss-it allusion to sex?
sentences.zh: 还有，你注意到他那狡黠的、几乎是潜意识的、一眨眼就会错过的性暗示了吗？

sentences.en: It was when she said they could have mad, passionate sex.
sentences.zh: 就是她说他们可以疯狂地做爱的时候。

sentences.en: So, what do you think, Aziz?
sentences.zh: 那么，阿齐兹，你怎么看？

sentences.en: Have these online technologies made us more prone to indiscretion and infidelity, or is this just a manifestation of how we've always been?
sentences.zh: 这些在线技术是否让我们更容易产生轻率和不忠的行为，还是说这只是我们本性的一贯表现？

sentences.en: I think it definitely, there's definitely, if you're trying to get involved in indiscretions, if you have these online things and you have your phone,
sentences.zh: 我认为绝对是这样，肯定有，如果你想搞点不正当关系，如果你有这些在线工具，还有你的手机，

sentences.en: if you have your phone, you have this very private world where you can conduct all sorts of s**t that no one knows about.
sentences.zh: 如果你有手机，你就拥有了一个非常私密的世界，可以在里面进行各种没人知道的勾当。

sentences.en: There's a story we tell in the book of this person who says they had a work colleague, and they were friendly with each other.
sentences.zh: 我们在书里讲过一个故事，有个人说他们有个同事，两人关系不错。

sentences.en: She was married, and she sent, like, a text message about something once, and it was, like, work-related, and he wrote back.
sentences.zh: 她结婚了，有一次她发了一条关于某事的短信，是工作相关的，他回了信。

sentences.en: And then, later, he saw something that was kind of funny that reminded him of her, and he sent a message, and they started joking back and forth.
sentences.zh: 后来，他看到了一些有趣的东西，想起了她，就发了条消息，他们开始互相开玩笑。

sentences.en: And this rapport started developing, and they eventually had this, like, very, like, intimate thing going on the phone where they were, like, having long conversations.
sentences.zh: 这种融洽的关系开始发展，最终他们在手机上进行了一些非常亲密的交流，比如长时间的通话。

sentences.en: And it became this very intimate thing, and it eventually led to some infidelity.
sentences.zh: 这变成了一种非常亲密的关系，最终导致了一些不忠行为。

sentences.en: And it was interesting because the guy was like, you know, if I didn't have text message, I wouldn't have sent that first message that started leading to that rapport.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那个家伙说，你知道吗，如果我没有短信，我就不会发那条导致这种关系开始的第一条消息。

sentences.en: You know, I would never have called her at her home and been like, hey, did you see that thing?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我绝不会打她家里的电话说，嘿，你看到那个东西了吗？

sentences.en: Like, you know, but with your phone, you can kind of build these kind of things that really escalate very quickly.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道的，但有了手机，你可以建立起那种升级非常迅速的关系。

sentences.en: And also, I think, like, you know, in the Anthony Weiner thing, it's like, oh, he's able to test the waters with that medium a little bit, where he's like, don't know,
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为，就像安东尼·韦纳那件事，他能够通过那种媒介稍微试探一下，他当时可能想，不知道，

sentences.en: make me an offer I can't refuse.
sentences.zh: 给我一个我无法拒绝的提议。

sentences.en: She could be like, oh, well, we'll go to Chili's.
sentences.zh: 她可能会说，哦，那我们去Chili's餐厅吧。

sentences.en: And he'll be like, oh, that doesn't sound fun.
sentences.zh: 他会说，哦，那听起来没意思。

sentences.en: But she immediately, like, got it and started getting sexual, and he knew, like, okay, this is a sexual thing.
sentences.zh: 但她立刻就明白了，开始变得色情起来，他知道，好吧，这是一件关于性的事。

sentences.en: She's down, and then after that message that I read, like, the floodgates opened, and then, you know, there was all the photos and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 她同意了，在那条我读过的消息之后，就像闸门打开了，然后，你知道，就有了所有的照片和那些东西。

sentences.en: You know, I don't think you can kind of accurately say whether it's led to an increase on the amount of infidelity that's going on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不认为你能准确地说这是否导致了不忠行为的增加。

sentences.en: I do think there's certain aspects of it that make it a little more, lend itself to it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为它的某些方面让这种情况更容易发生，是的。

sentences.en: One of the things you talk about in the book is about how online dating is rapidly becoming the way many people meet.
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到的一件事是关于在线约会如何迅速成为许多人相识的方式。

sentences.en: But you also find that this is especially true for same-sex couples, that same-sex couples, online dating has really become the dominant way people meet one another.
sentences.zh: 但你也发现这对同性伴侣尤其如此，对于同性伴侣来说，在线约会确实已成为人们相识的主导方式。

sentences.en: Why do you think that's going on, or what do you think it means?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么会这样，或者你认为这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, that is about something, a phenomenon related to what are referred to as thin markets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这与所谓的“薄市场”现象有关。

sentences.en: You know, I spoke with this woman who, like, late in her life, like, she was married to a guy, and then she got divorced and just kind of decided, like, you know what,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我采访过一位女士，她晚年时，曾嫁给一个男人，后来离婚了，就决定，你知道吗，

sentences.en: I'm a lesbian.
sentences.zh: 我是个女同性恋。

sentences.en: Like, I've been a lesbian my whole life, and she lives in this small town in Texas, and she started online dating and going out on dates and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 就像，我这辈子都是女同性恋，她住在德克萨斯州的一个小镇上，她开始在线约会，出去约会之类的。

sentences.en: And I thought about that, and I was like, wow, like, if that was her, you know, 20, 30 years ago, that would have been a much different thing.
sentences.zh: 我思考过这件事，我想，哇，如果那是20、30年前的她，那情况会大不相同。

sentences.en: You know, being in a place like Texas, in a small town where maybe people aren't as open to that kind of stuff, it would have been way harder.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在德克萨斯州这样的小镇，人们可能对那种事情没那么开放，那会困难得多。

sentences.en: Whereas now, she can go online, and she's able to meet people, and it's really a huge event for her.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她可以上网，能够结识别人，这对她来说真的是一件大事。

sentences.en: So, this is in some way sort of the positive side of technology, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，这在某种程度上是技术的积极一面，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it allows people who have minority interests, if you will, or sort of special interests, not to be lonely forever, to actually find people who match their interests,
sentences.zh: 因为它允许那些有少数群体兴趣，或者说特殊兴趣的人，不必永远孤独，能够真正找到与他们兴趣相投的人，

sentences.en: match their needs.
sentences.zh: 满足他们的需求。

sentences.en: And this is what technology has enabled.
sentences.zh: 这就是技术所带来的。

sentences.en: It's really helped in those kind of in markets or whatever.
sentences.zh: 它确实在那些市场或其他方面提供了帮助。

sentences.en: And I think it's a good point that, like, for all these things, I feel like, you know, if kind of one of the big questions the book is asking is, oh, is all this stuff good or bad?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个很好的观点，就像对于所有这些事情，我觉得，你知道，如果这本书提出的一个大问题是，哦，所有这些东西是好是坏？

sentences.en: And I think for each thing, it's not one answer.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于每一件事，都没有单一的答案。

sentences.en: It's both.
sentences.zh: 两者兼有。

sentences.en: It really just depends on how you use these tools.
sentences.zh: 这真的取决于你如何使用这些工具。

sentences.en: You know, something like online dating, there's one notion of, like, oh, everyone's on their phones, everyone thinks that there's something better out there,
sentences.zh: 你知道，像在线约会这样的事情，有一种观点是，哦，每个人都在玩手机，每个人都觉得外面有更好的选择，

sentences.en: and it's just added so much stress to my life, and I hate it.
sentences.zh: 这给我的生活增加了太多的压力，我讨厌它。

sentences.en: Then, you could also look at the other side of, like, well, one out of three people that get married now, they meet their spouse through online dating.
sentences.zh: 然后，你也可以看看另一面，比如，现在每三对结婚的人中就有一对是通过在线约会认识的。

sentences.en: And a huge percentage of these people are meeting people that they would not have met had it not been for these sites.
sentences.zh: 而且这些人中有很大一部分遇到的人，如果不是因为这些网站，他们根本不会相遇。

sentences.en: So you could look at it like, oh, well, there's an insane amount of new love in the world that's created because of this technology.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以这样看，哦，好吧，因为这项技术，世界上创造了海量的新爱情。

sentences.en: And there's just this overwhelming amount of love that would not even be there had it not been for these things.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些东西，甚至都不会有这么多压倒性的爱。

sentences.en: And I feel like you can't deny that that's a positive thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你不能否认这是一件积极的事情。

sentences.en: That's comedian Aziz Ansari.
sentences.zh: 那是喜剧演员阿齐兹·安萨里。

sentences.en: His book, written with the sociologist Eric Kleinenberg, is modern romance.
sentences.zh: 他与社会学家埃里克·克莱南伯格合著的书是《现代浪漫》。

sentences.en: If you like this show, can you do us a favor?
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这个节目，能帮我们一个忙吗？

sentences.en: Go to iTunes and give us a rating.
sentences.zh: 去iTunes给我们打个分。

sentences.en: This will help other people find our show.
sentences.zh: 这会帮助其他人找到我们的节目。

sentences.en: In fact, if you drop the word jam into your review, we'll know you came from this episode.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你在评论中加入“jam”这个词，我们就会知道你是从这一集来的。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain Podcast is produced by Kara McGurk-Allison, Maggie Penman, and Max Nestrack.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》播客由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森、玛吉·彭曼和马克斯·内斯特拉克制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Daniel Shukin and Jay Sizz.
sentences.zh: 本周特别感谢丹尼尔·舒金和杰伊·西兹。

sentences.en: For more Hidden Brain, find us on Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram, and listen to my stories on your local public radio station.
sentences.zh: 想了解更多《隐藏的大脑》，请在Facebook、Twitter和Instagram上关注我们，并在当地公共广播电台收听我的故事。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，这是NPR。
